notes: ὀρθός takes upright and Ἀνάστηθι takes Stand alone; the ASV's order puts upright before on thy feet, which rule 15 permits.
ἅλλομαι carries no preverb, so the up of leaped up is English phrasal idiom riding inside the verb's unit as a rule 7 helper rather than a rule 106 preverb particle.
τούς is unrepresented under rule 20, the determiner slot being occupied by thy, which belongs to σου.
